title: Septic Service Checklist
subtitle: Residential Septic Service: documents findings, limits, and disposition.
description: Septic Service Checklist covers tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area. The septic service coordinator records Residential Septic Service criteria, findings, restrictions, and follow-up. Septic Service Checklist keeps Residential Septic Service exceptions visible until the septic service coordinator handoff.
use_case: Use Septic Service Checklist at property, tank access, pump chamber, distribution area, and protected ground surface. Document tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area identity before Residential Septic Service begins. Compare tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area findings with stated Residential Septic Service criteria; route unresolved Residential Septic Service issues to qualified septic-system reviewer. For Septic Service Checklist, confirm requirements for Residential Septic Service. Ask qualified septic-system reviewer to review Residential Septic Service conditions beyond the septic service coordinator's role.

sections.title: Checklist context and subject record
sections.guidance: For Residential Septic Service, identify responsible parties, property, tank access, pump chamber, distribution area, and protected ground surface, and the linked tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area source.

fields.label: System type, tank or component identifier, and access point
Occupancy, last service, symptom, and weather history

sections.title: Checklist points, conditions, and actions
sections.guidance: Capture Residential Septic Service facts for tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area; include result, limit, source, and next control.

blocks.label: Residential Septic Service inspection checks
items: Access cover, riser, seal, and surface condition
Liquid level, scum, sludge, inlet, outlet, and baffle observation
Pump, float, alarm, control, and electrical indication
Backup, odor, surfacing effluent, and wet-area evidence
Vehicle, excavation, fall, biological, and confined-space boundary
Post-service level, closure, alarm, and flow observation

columns.label: Pass, issue, N/A, or not inspected

sections.title: Inspection exception, restriction, and reinspection
sections.guidance: Before closing Residential Septic Service, identify what failed or was not inspected, who owns correction, and when examination resumes. Septic Service Coordinator preserves the decision.

blocks.label: Deficiencies, restrictions, and retained evidence
items: Unsafe opening, fall, biological, or confined-space exposure
Backup or surfacing effluent threatens occupancy
Damaged tank or component requires excavation
Electrical, structural, or regulatory work outside scope
Cover closure, alarm, and customer restriction evidence
blocks.guidance: Pause Residential Septic Service when access safety, containment, backup, structural integrity, disposal, or qualified escalation remains unresolved. Retain the available Residential Septic Service proof and route unresolved tank, inlet, outlet, baffle, pump, alarm, distribution component, and disposal area scope to septic service coordinator.
